etymologies.etymologyHTML: From outside +‎ -er.

definitions.definition: One who is not part of a community or organization.

quote.citation: 2004, George Carlin, “Preface”, in When Will Jesus Bring the Pork Chops?‎[1], New York: Hyperion Books, →ISBN, →OCLC, →OL, page [2]:
quote.text: I'm an outsider by choice, but not truly. It's the unpleasantness of the system that keeps me out. I'd rather be in, in a good system. That's where my discontent comes from: being forced to choose to stay outside.

quote.citation: 2019, Victor C. de Munck, Romantic Love in America, page 152:
quote.text: We were not a big huggie family so I was very, very encased in a little stay-away-from-me shell growing-up, and here I got to open up and feel safe and able to touch and hold and be able to be with another human being, which was really a big relief, a very positive part of my understanding of myself that I wasn't just this outcast evil outsider of everything.

definitions.definition: A newcomer with little or no experience in an organization or community.

quote.citation: 2017, BioWare, Mass Effect: Andromeda (Science Fiction), Redwood City: Electronic Arts, →OCLC, PC, scene: Legacy:
quote.text: These worlds have always belonged to us, from the moment our ancestors saw them through ancient telescopes. We claimed them when our first explorers reached the stars, and they remained our worlds even after the Scourge divided us in darkness. Outsiders have no right to these treasures, and true angara must stand ready to defend our birthright.

definitions.definition: A competitor or contestant who has little chance of winning; a long shot.
